references.text: God saw that Leah was hated, so he opened her womb, while Rachel was barren
God remembered Rachel; he listened to her and opened her womb
Isaac prayed to the Lord for his wife because she was barren. The Lord answered his prayer, and Rebekah conceived
Sarai, Abram's wife, had borne him no children. She had an Egyptian slave named Hagar
Children are a heritage from the Lord, offspring a reward
Hannah was barren, and Peninnah provoked her continually because the Lord had closed her womb
Jacob became angry with Rachel and said, 'Am I in God's place, who has withheld children from you?'
Contrast between Rachel's fear of dying childless and her grief over her children being gone.
Direct continuation of the conflict over children and a husband's love within the same narrative.
Matthew quotes Jeremiah, who again refers to Rachel's role in Genesis.
